work.name: Advanced Particle Detector Laboratory (APDL)
highlights: Led a team of 3 interns to develop Machine Learning algorithms for auto-focus, depth perception, and filtered back propagation, advancing capabilities in Muon Tomography.
Achieved 87% accuracy in muon hit prediction by designing an Asymmetric Deep Mixture Density Neural Network based on photon time propagation data.
Created a 3D reconstruction algorithm using CNNs and dynamic k-means clustering for improved spatial resolution and image segmentation.
Built and deployed Monte Carlo simulations (Geant4, ROOT) and automated Python-based analysis to validate data integrity, assess design efficiency, and measure telescope performance.
Conducted simulations on muon scattering and absorption to refine imaging quality and optimize parameter settings.
Refactored and deployed lab software on the High Performance Computing (HPC) Cluster, boosting processing speed and resource utilization.
Calibrated and installed 40 SiPMs (Phase 1) and 44 PMTs (Phase 2) on telescopes, enhancing precision and operational reliability.
Designed custom PCBs (KiCAD, LTspice) and CNC-machined Winston Cone light collectors, significantly improving optical transmission and signal quality.

work.name: Texas Tech University
work.summary: Introduction to Quantum Information and Computation (QIC)
highlights: Delivered supplemental lecture notes and interactive Jupyter notebooks, teaching quantum computing through IBM's Qiskit to enhance hands-on learning.
Developed bi-weekly computational assignments, covering foundational Quantum Information and Computing topics to reinforce students' technical understanding.
Provided weekly office hours, offering targeted support for problem-solving and conceptual understanding.
Graded computational and theoretical assignments for over 25 students, ensuring fair and thorough assessment across the cohort.
Guided and collaborated with students on semester research projects, fostering research-oriented thinking and applied problem-solving.

Covered topics included: Qiskit API, single and multi-qubit systems, statevector evolution, superposition and entanglement, quantum circuit model, quantum teleportation, and advanced algorithms like Deutsch's and Grover's Algorithms.

work.name: University of Southern California
work.summary: Fundamentals of Physics II: Electricity and Magnetism
highlights: Voted Best TA by students for two consecutive semesters, recognized for commitment to student learning and support.
Led lab sessions for 36 undergraduate engineering students, mentoring them in experimental applications of the course
Facilitated hands-on lab exercises covering physical circuit implementation, EM fields, potentials, Gauss' law, and Faraday's law to solidify theoretical knowledge through practical experience.
Provided training on oscilloscopes, function generators, and analysis of RC & LC circuits, transformers, and toroids, and conducted experiments to study resonance and measure Planck's constant.
Ensured high-quality learning experiences by overseeing lab safety, fostering analytical skills, and providing individualized support to optimize student performance.

work.name: Institute for Software Integrated Systems (ISIS), Vanderbilt University
highlights: Designed memory efficient computational models for various microscopic traffic simulations using C++, Python, Bash, and XML
Developed a system for calibrating stochastic simulation results using multi-objective methods and gradient-free algorithms, enhancing model accuracy and data reliability.
Integrated Ray to parallelize simulations, resulting in significant performance gains and enabling the handling of large-scale experiments with improved runtime efficiency.
Created scripts to convert microscopic data from the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) into radar-style (RDS) formats.
Implemented custom optimization routines to align simulation outputs with macroscopic RDS datasets, increasing fidelity and validating simulations against real-world data.
Collaborated with a multidisciplinary team and delivered findings to senior researchers, influencing ongoing research in I-24 MOTION and the CIRCLES Consortium.
Contributed to Flow (by UC Berkeley), a deep reinforcement learning framework for traffic microsimulation.
Published research in a conference proceeding, presenting innovative calibration techniques for microsimulation models, with applications in traffic flow optimization and sensor calibration.
